areas.body:
## Window cleaning across Market Drayton

From terraces and cottages near the town centre to the newer estates on the edge of town, we clean every kind of home in Market Drayton. Danny started cleaning windows here at 18 with a ladder and a bucket. Today DEC uses a pure-water system and a long water-fed pole, so upstairs windows get cleaned from the ground and nobody is leaning a ladder against your guttering.

## Why the water matters here

Market Drayton's mains water is classed as hard. Clean with tap water and the minerals dry on the glass as spots and streaks. We clean with water that has had almost everything filtered out of it, so it dries clear with no soap left behind. [Read more about hard water and streaky windows](/blog/hard-water-streaky-windows/).

## How often?

For most homes in town, every 4 weeks keeps windows looking right. Homes on busy roads or near trees may want it a little more often, and quieter spots can stretch to 6 to 8 weeks. [Here's how to work out the right frequency for your home](/blog/how-often-should-windows-be-cleaned/).

faq.q: Do I need to be home for my window clean?
faq.a: No. As long as we can get to the windows, including any side gate, we can clean while you're out. You'll get a text the day before so you know we're coming.

faq.q: How much does window cleaning cost in Market Drayton?
faq.a: Regular cleans start from £14 for a smaller semi-detached home. The exact price depends on the type of property and the number of bedrooms, and our online calculator shows yours in about 30 seconds. First cleans and one-off cleans carry a surcharge.

## Window cleaning in Loggerheads and the parish

Loggerheads grew quickly through the 20th century, and much of the village is family homes with plenty of glass: detached houses, bungalows and extensions. We clean all of it, along with homes in Ashley, Mucklestone, Hookgate, Almington and Hales.

## Homes near Burntwood

If you back on to Burntwood or have mature trees nearby, your windows will collect more pollen, sap and tree dust than a house in the middle of town. Our water-fed brush scrubs the frames and sills as well as the glass, so the grime that builds up around the edges goes too, not just the bit in the middle.

## Out of county, same service

Being in Staffordshire makes no difference to us. You get the same price list as Market Drayton, the same text the day before each visit, and the same online customer portal where you can see your next clean and move dates around.

faq.q: Do you really cover Loggerheads? It's in Staffordshire.
faq.a: Yes. Loggerheads uses the Market Drayton post town and is a few minutes up the A53. We cover the village and the surrounding parish, including Ashley, Mucklestone and Hookgate.

faq.q: Is there a travel charge for Loggerheads?
faq.a: No. Prices are the same as in Market Drayton. Use the online calculator to see yours.

## Window cleaning in Hinstock

Hinstock has a real mix of homes: older cottages near St Oswald's and the village centre, family houses, and properties out towards Pixley and High Heath. We clean them all, including conservatories, porches and the awkward upstairs windows above extensions.

## Road dust and the A41

The A41 bypasses the village now, but homes close to the A41 and A529 still pick up traffic film on the glass, a grey haze that ordinary rain doesn't shift. Pure water and a soft brush lift it off without soap, so there's no residue left behind for the next shower to streak.

## Booking from Hinstock

Put your house type and bedrooms into the calculator to get an instant price. Then send it over, or just text or WhatsApp Danny on 07367 298 499.

faq.q: How often should windows be cleaned in Hinstock?
faq.a: Every 4 weeks suits most homes. If you're close to the main roads or have lots of trees, you might want it a little more often. Quieter spots can stretch to 6 to 8 weeks.

faq.q: Can you clean my conservatory too?
faq.a: Yes. Conservatory glass can be added to your regular clean, and the calculator includes it. For a full roof clean, send us a photo and we'll quote.

areas.body:
## Window cleaning in Norton-in-Hales

From the cottages around the green and St Chad's to farmhouses and family homes out towards Betton and Ridgwardine, Norton-in-Hales has a lot of character, and a lot of older windows. We take care with them.

## Gentle on older and painted frames

Pure-water cleaning uses no detergent and no squeegee dragged across old putty or painted timber. A soft brush on a water-fed pole scrubs the glass and frames, then everything gets rinsed with filtered water that dries clear. That suits period windows, and upstairs windows get done from the ground without ladders against old walls.

## Rural homes, longer gaps

Homes in open countryside often pick up less traffic grime than town houses, so some customers here are happy with a clean every 6 to 8 weeks. If you're near fields that are being worked, every 4 weeks keeps things tidy.

faq.q: Will pure-water cleaning damage older timber windows?
faq.a: No. It uses only filtered water and a soft brush, with no soap or harsh chemicals, which makes it one of the gentler ways to clean painted and older frames.

faq.q: Do you cover Betton and Ridgwardine?
faq.a: Yes, along with the rest of Norton-in-Hales parish.

## Window cleaning in Moreton Say

Moreton Say has no shops and a lot of fields. Many homes are farmhouses, converted barns and houses set back down long lanes. That's no problem for us. We bring the water with us, so we don't need an outside tap, and we cover the hamlets too: Longford, Longslow, Bletchley and Styche.

## Farm dust and big windows

Homes surrounded by working fields pick up dust at harvest and muck-spreading time, and barn conversions often have large glazed gable ends that are hard to reach. Our water-fed pole reaches high glass safely from the ground and scrubs the frames as well, so the dust that settles there doesn't wash back down the window the next time it rains.

## Fitting round you

You don't need to be in. You'll get a text the day before each visit, and you can see your next clean in your online customer portal.

faq.q: Do you need to use my water or electricity?
faq.a: No. We bring our own purified water with us, so we don't need an outside tap or a power socket.

faq.q: Can you reach tall barn-conversion windows?
faq.a: Usually yes. The water-fed pole reaches high glass from the ground. If you're not sure, send us a photo and we'll tell you.
